title: User recipe (v1)
description:
Schema for `.tera/users/<name>.hcl` recipes per [ADR-135](../adr/ADR-135-the-near-side-issuer-and-work-on-behalf-of-a-person.md) D5. A **user** is a person the deployment has to *say something about*, and the kind is deliberately the exception rather than the rule: D12 provisions a person on SSO on first login into a runtime store beside the token vault, and **that store is not this kind and never becomes a file in a vault**. Three cases earn a file — a local user with a password, which is the no-IdP golden path; a person outside an identity provider's `allowed_domains` an admin wants to admit; and an SSO user an admin wants to pre-declare, to give them groups before their first login or to link them to an existing local record.

**The record carries a digest and never a secret.** `password_hash` is an argon2id PHC string — `tera auth user add` writes it and never writes the password it hashed — in the digest-in-config shape the `static` authenticator's `api_key { key_hash }` already takes. It is deliberately NOT bcrypt, which is what `static { user { password_hash } }` and the `file` authenticator use: those two surfaces are unchanged, and a bcrypt digest in this field is refused at load naming bcrypt, because it is the wrong digest this tree makes easy to reach for and it would otherwise fail later as a wrong password for a person who typed the right one.

**A password hash and an identity block may both be present**, and that is the supported linked state (D11) rather than a conflict — so this is NOT a union and carries no `oneof` tag. The one rule is that a record with NEITHER is refused at load, naming the file: such a record cannot be authenticated by any route, now or after a provider is configured, so it is not a person who cannot log in yet but a declaration with no content.

**The provider's stable subject is never written back into the file.** An `identity` block matches on `email` at first login and the daemon records the subject daemon-side, so no login ever writes a recipe — which is what keeps the kind on the right side of `tera config apply`, where a reconcile can only ever delete what an operator declared. The `identity` block is consumed at first login: a login at the named provider whose address matches it, and whose provider asserts `email_verified` true for that address, resolves to this record, and an unverified address binds nothing. The block's label references an `identity_provider` declared on the issuer and is validated for SHAPE only, because resolving it at load would refuse exactly the pre-declared SSO user this kind's third case exists for, which is authored before the provider it names.

The file stem is the identity, so `alice.hcl` declares the record `alice`. The recipe declares a single `user` block whose label must equal that stem.

version.description: Per-recipe grammar version. Required; this schema applies when version is v1.

name.description: Bare user name (the HCL block label), which must equal the filename stem. The loader namespaces the recipe as <vault-id>/users/<name>, and the stem is this record DURABLE key: the runtime store assigns the opaque tera-issued id against it, so the id survives a restart, a reload and an edit to any other field on the record. That is ADR-135 D2 made concrete - the id is what the token vault keys on and what audit stores, so an email change must not mint a new principal.

email.description: The address this person is known by. It is a CLAIM and not the principal (ADR-135 D2): the principal is the record opaque tera-issued id, and the email is what people see and write, and what a role binding names when it binds this person by email. The load-time check is deliberately shallow - non-empty and containing an @ - because what is refused is a value no operator would recognise as an address, not one a mail server would bounce; a stricter grammar would refuse legitimate addresses while establishing nothing about the person, and it is the provider that decides what its own subjects addresses look like.

display_name.description: What to call this person in a listing. Optional; a consumer renders the email in its place rather than inventing a name from the stem.

groups.description: Groups this record carries (ADR-135 D6). It is the one place to grant admins that works for a local user, for a Google login that returns no groups, and for an enterprise provider that does - a role binding idp_group then reaches all three. For a person who also logs in through a provider these are MERGED with whatever groups the provider sends, and where a recipe names the same email as an auto-created runtime record the RECIPE is authoritative (D5). NOTHING IN THE RECIPE STAMPS A GROUP ONTO A LIVE IDENTITY: per ADR-116 D1 the directory groups reach a token only through the issuer authentication event, so this field is what a record DECLARES and never what a caller was granted. Order is the author, repeats are dropped.

password_hash.description: The argon2id digest a local login is verified against, as a PHC string ($argon2id$v=19$m=...,t=...,p=...$salt$key). Optional: a record may instead - or also - declare identity blocks. THE RECIPE HOLDS A DIGEST AND NEVER A PASSWORD, and tera auth user add writes the digest without ever writing what it hashed; the shape is the one the static authenticator api_key key_hash already takes. ARGON2ID IS RULED BY D5 AND BCRYPT IS REFUSED BY NAME - bcrypt is what static { user { password_hash } } and the file authenticator use and it is therefore the wrong digest this tree makes easy to paste, and it would fail at login as a wrong password for a person who typed the right one rather than failing where it was written. The cost parameters travel inside the string, so raising them for new passwords does not invalidate the digests already written. Writing the attribute blank is refused rather than read as absence: an author who wrote it believes this record has a password.

identity.description: Zero or more links to a remote identity provider, one per provider. An admin STATING the link in a file, which is why it does not conflict with ADR-135 D11 - what D11 refuses is a LOGIN silently attaching itself to a record, and auto-merge on matching email is a classic account-takeover hole refused by name. The block label references an identity_provider declared on the issuer. CONSUMED AT FIRST LOGIN: a verified login at the named provider whose address matches this block, and whose provider asserts email_verified true for that address, resolves to THIS record - an address the provider has not verified is one its holder merely typed, and binds nothing - and the daemon records which of the provider subjects it was in its own store - the file is never written, so tera config apply and the login path never contend over it. Two remote identities cannot share one record at one provider: once a subject is recorded here, a second one asserting the same address is refused rather than attached, because it is the same takeover D11 refuses arriving through the provider instead of through the email. The label is still validated for SHAPE ONLY (non-empty, one bare segment, no whitespace) and is deliberately NOT resolved against a configured provider at load, because the pre-declared SSO user this kind third case exists for is authored before the provider it names. Two blocks with the same label are refused: they are two answers to which remote identity at that provider this person is, and first login would settle it by decode order.

provider.description: The identity_provider this link is at (the block label). A reference to a provider declared on the issuer. The label is checked for shape and deliberately not resolved at load: a provider declared after the user recipe that names it is the authoring order this kind third case exists for, so refusing an unresolved label would refuse the pre-declared SSO user.

email.description: The address matched at this provider on first login, after which the recorded subject is what resolves the person and this address is only a claim - so a provider that later changes it does not detach the link or move the record opaque id. THE PROVIDER STABLE SUBJECT IS NOT HERE AND DOES NOT BELONG HERE: ADR-135 D5 records it daemon-side in the runtime store, so a recipe is never edited by a login - which is what keeps this kind on the right side of tera config apply, where a reconcile can only ever delete what an operator declared. A field for the subject would put the apply path and the login path in a write race over one file.
